Text:
Independence Palace, at 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, combines historical interpretation with architectural observation. Consider the grounds, the arrangement of spaces and the functions of its rooms alongside the familiar façade.

Architect Ngo Viet Thu designed the present palace. Construction began in 1962 and it opened in 1966. The design combines modern spatial planning with ideas from East Asian culture. Look at the decorative stone screen on the second floor, whose shapes suggest bamboo stems. The palace is associated with the events of April 30, 1975, and was designated a special national historical site in 2009.

The managing institution explains the overall plan through the Chinese character for good fortune and identifies the Presentation of Credentials Room as its centre. This adds a way to read the building: move from its exterior form to the order of its spaces and the ceremonies associated with them.

Connect three strands during your visit: architecture, function and historical context. Observe the façade's proportions, read the labels in accessible rooms and compare them with exhibition material. This is a suggested method of exploration, not a promise that every room or route is open.

Read the information panels and follow the current visitor route. After each room, recall its function and one architectural detail. Linking these observations creates an ordered account of the visit; protect the exhibits and respect restricted areas.
